qa.verdict: Spec is NOT ready for dev: 6 blockers found across AC2 (backward compat gap), AC10/AC17 (deselect semantic conflict), AC20/M20 (client-only vs server origin_slot_id), AC24/Hint-19 (required-slot set contradiction), AC17/persistence (no save mutation specified for source clear), and validators.py stage-gate conflict with AC24.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex confirmed all 4 QA-identified blockers (Findings 1, 2, 5, 7) and added 2 new blockers (M17 persistence underspecified; validators.py stage-gate contract mismatch) plus 2 warnings (origin attribute naming drift; mobile breakpoint boundary ambiguity). Codex also upgraded Finding 5: 'set null explicitly' is insufficient because `null ?? persistedId` still falls back — AC10's ?? operator conflicts with AC17's clearing semantics.
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: All Codex PROPOSED_FIX items evaluated. Blockers 1-6 all incorporated into this report. Two Codex warnings incorporated as warnings W1-W2. No Codex finding rejected.

blockers.title: Required-slot definition contradiction: AC24 specifies 4 slots; Hint 19 references a 7-slot function
blockers.description: AC24 (ticket line 420-430) defines required slots as 'accommodation + breakfast + lunch + dinner' (4 slots). Technical Hint 19 says 'mirror _allRequiredSlotsFilled from web/js/state.js — iterate ALL_SLOT_KEYS'. But ALL_SLOT_KEYS = NAMED_SLOTS.concat(['accommodation']) = [breakfast, morning_activity, lunch, afternoon_activity, dinner, evening_activity, accommodation] — 7 slots. The function _allRequiredSlotsFilled (state.js:604-610) does NOT call _isRequiredSlot (state.js:562-565); _isRequiredSlot is a separate, unused helper within that function. If dev mirrors _allRequiredSlotsFilled literally, the Approve button will be disabled whenever any ACTIVITY slot (morning_activity, afternoon_activity, evening_activity) is unfilled or absent, directly violating AC24's intent.

evidence.hint19_text: mirror _allRequiredSlotsFilled from web/js/state.js — iterate ALL_SLOT_KEYS (ticket line ~532)
evidence.state_js_named_slots: web/js/state.js:22-29 — NAMED_SLOTS = [breakfast, morning_activity, lunch, afternoon_activity, dinner, evening_activity]
evidence.state_js_isrequiredslot: web/js/state.js:562-565 — separate helper, checks accommodation or MEAL_SLOTS

blockers.proposed_fix: Replace Technical Hint 19 with explicit required-only logic: 'const REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS = ["accommodation", "breakfast", "lunch", "dinner"]; implement allRequiredSlotsFilled iterating only REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS — NOT ALL_SLOT_KEYS'. Add an AC24 positive edge case: 'GIVEN accommodation/breakfast/lunch/dinner are filled AND morning_activity is absent or unfilled, WHEN Approve renders, THEN Approve is enabled (if stage is draft-options or user-review)'. Apply same required-only gating to AC26 export button validation.

blockers.title: AC20 'client-side only, no backend call' conflicts with save.py origin_slot_id persistence path
blockers.description: AC20 says cross-meal copy is 'client-side-only idempotent copy; no backend change'. However, scripts/lib/server/save.py:_apply_select_mutation (lines 75-104) already implements server-side cross-meal option copy when origin_slot_id is provided in the mutation. The current window.setEditorSelection bridge (react_template.tpl:1924) sends origin_slot_id: null, disabling the server copy. The new React model must decide: (a) purely client-side in editorSelections state only — but then after a page reload the server-side persisted day data will NOT have the option in dinner.options[], causing a broken state; OR (b) pass origin_slot_id in the /api/save mutation — but AC20 says 'no backend call'. The two approaches are mutually exclusive and the spec does not resolve which. Without the origin_slot_id in the save payload, a user drops a breakfast option onto dinner, it appears selected in the session, but on reload dinner.options is missing the option and the selection disappears.

evidence.ac20_text: client-side-only idempotent copy; no backend API call is made for the copy (ticket line 375-382)
evidence.save_py_cross_meal_copy: scripts/lib/server/save.py:81-103 — _apply_select_mutation performs copy when origin_slot_id is set and both slots are meal slots
evidence.react_bridge_origin_null: scripts/lib/react_template.tpl:1924 — origin_slot_id: null (hardcoded null in current bridge)

blockers.proposed_fix: Clarify AC20 to: 'The frontend copies the option object into the target slot's editorSelections or editorTripData state (client-side only for the in-session view). The /api/save mutation for this selection MUST include origin_slot_id so the existing server-side save.py persistence logic can durably copy the option into the target slot's options[] for persistence across reloads. This is NOT a new backend change — save.py already handles origin_slot_id.' Also add a reload durability test: 'GIVEN option X selected from breakfast dropped onto dinner, WHEN page is reloaded, THEN dinner still shows X as selected and dinner.options[] contains X.'

blockers.title: deselect semantics conflict: AC17 clearing with AC10's ?? fallback operator makes null set insufficient
blockers.description: AC17 says plan→candidates drag 'clears that slot's selected_option_id'. AC10/M9 specifies that the selected candidate is identified by 'editorSelections[dayKey + ":" + slotId] ?? slot.selected_option_id'. If dev sets editorSelections[key] = null to deselect, the ?? operator will fall through to slot.selected_option_id (the published/persisted value), which may be non-null — so the slot will STILL appear selected. Setting to null is not sufficient; deleting the key causes the same problem (key absent -> ?? -> falls back to published value). AC10 and AC17 create an unresolvable conflict: the ?? operator needed for AC10's fallback behavior makes AC17's deselection impossible without changing the lookup semantics.

evidence.ac17_clear: that slot's selected_option_id is cleared (ticket line 350)
evidence.null_coalescence: JavaScript: null ?? 'persistedId' === 'persistedId' — null does NOT prevent fallback with ?? operator

blockers.proposed_fix: Change AC10 lookup to use key-presence semantics instead of ??: 'const key = dayKey + ":" + slotId; const selectedId = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(editorSelections, key) ? editorSelections[key] : slot.selected_option_id'. Then AC17 deselect = set editorSelections[key] = null (explicit null, key present). AC10's fallback to published value only fires when key is ABSENT (never explicitly set). Update M9/AC10 text to reflect hasOwnProperty semantics rather than ?? operator.

blockers.title: AC2 requires two positional args for generate_html but does not mandate trip_id=None default, leaving generate-html-interactive.py:598 as a guaranteed runtime crash
blockers.description: AC2 (ticket line 220-226) specifies 'generate_html signature is generate_html(gen, trip_id) (two positional args)'. The existing caller at scripts/generate-html-interactive.py:598 calls _bld.generate_html(self) with ONE positional arg. If dev implements two required positional args, this call site will raise a TypeError at runtime. Technical Hint 1 (ticket line 496) mentions this risk: 'generate_html should accept trip_id=None as default OR that call site must also be updated'. However, AC2 does not REQUIRE either the default OR updating the call site — it only specifies the signature. An AC that does not mandate safe behavior is unenforceable: dev can pass AC2 with two required positional args and break the existing call site without violating any AC.

evidence.ac2_signature: generate_html signature is generate_html(gen, trip_id) (two positional args) (ticket line 224)
evidence.existing_caller: scripts/generate-html-interactive.py:598 calls _bld.generate_html(self) with one arg (context JSON component_chain)
evidence.hint1_risk: Technical Hint 1 mentions trip_id=None or updating call site — but AC2 does not require either (ticket line 496)

blockers.proposed_fix: Update AC2 to explicitly require: 'generate_html signature is generate_html(gen, trip_id=None) with trip_id defaulting to None; OR all call sites are updated to pass trip_id; AND scripts/generate-html-interactive.py must still execute successfully after the change.' Preferred: add trip_id=None default.

blockers.title: AC17 bidirectional drag describes UI state clearing but does not specify required /api/save mutations for source slot clear — reload will resurrect deselected cards
blockers.description: AC17 specifies that plan→candidates drag 'clears that slot's selected_option_id' and slot→slot move 'clears slot A's selected_option_id'. This describes React state change only. The spec does NOT require a /api/save mutation to persist the source slot clear. If only editorSelections state is updated without a backend save for the source clear, a page reload will resurrect the previously placed card in the source slot (because the server-side day JSON still has selected_option_id set). Codex flagged this as a blocker.

evidence.ac17_text: slot A's selected_option_id is cleared AND slot B's selected_option_id is set in a single state update (ticket line 353)
evidence.missing_save_spec: No /api/save mutation requirement for source slot clear anywhere in AC17, M17, or Technical Hint 11
evidence.reload_risk: Server day JSON retains old selected_option_id; on reload effectiveDay merges from server state, not editorSelections

blockers.proposed_fix: Add to AC17: 'For plan→candidates: the frontend sends POST /api/save with mutation { type: "select", slot: sourceSlotId, option_id: null } to clear the server-side selection; for slot→slot: the frontend sends POST /api/save with a batch mutation clearing source and setting destination in a single request. The save must complete before the deselection is considered durable.'

blockers.title: validators.py stage-gate contract checks ALL 7 slots, conflicting with AC24 required-only definition — approving a day via AC8 with unfilled activity slots will trigger STAGE_GATE_VIOLATION
blockers.description: scripts/lib/trip_contract/validators.py:_check_stage_gate (lines 347-365) checks that when stage >= user-selected, 'every non-skipped slot must have selected_option_id' — it iterates NAMED_SLOTS + [ACCOMMODATION_SLOT] (all 7 slots). AC24 says the Approve button is enabled when only accommodation + breakfast + lunch + dinner are filled. This means a user can approve a day (per AC24) with empty morning_activity/afternoon_activity/evening_activity, but the validator will then reject the save mutation with STAGE_GATE_VIOLATION because the activity slots are unfilled. The backend and the frontend spec are directly contradictory.

evidence.validators_py_message: stage='user-selected' requires non-skipped slot 'morning_activity' to have selected_option_id
evidence.ac24_enable_condition: all non-skipped required slots (accommodation, breakfast, lunch, or dinner) have a selected_option_id (ticket line 425)

blockers.proposed_fix: BA must resolve the conflict between validators.py and AC24 before dev starts. Two options: (1) Update validators.py stage-gate to only check required slots (accommodation, breakfast, lunch, dinner) — non-required activity slots are not gated. (2) Update AC24/M24 to require ALL non-skipped slots across all 7 slot types to be filled before Approve is enabled, matching the current validator. This is a BA/PM decision; do not leave divergent.

warnings.title: origin attribute naming drift: Hint 11 says data-origin-slot; M19 says data-origin-slot-id; drag.js uses dataset.originSlotId
warnings.description: M19 (ticket line 122) specifies each meal card carries 'data-origin-slot-id=<source slot key>'. Technical Hint 11 says 'the dragstart handler must set data-origin-slot on the payload' — missing the -id suffix. The existing drag.js reads dataset.originSlotId (camelCase from data-origin-slot-id). These are inconsistent. If dev follows Hint 11 and uses data-origin-slot, drag.js would read it as dataset.originSlot (undefined) and origin_slot_id would always be null.
warnings.proposed_fix: Correct Technical Hint 11 to use data-origin-slot-id (with -id suffix), matching M19 and existing drag.js behavior.

warnings.title: Mobile breakpoint boundary ambiguity at 768px — AC13 does not specify boundary-inclusive behavior
warnings.description: M12 says isMobileLayout = window.innerWidth < 768. AC13 tests at 390px (mobile) and 1440px (desktop) but does not specify what happens at exactly 768px. The spec notes that existing useBreakpoint() returns 'sm' at <640px — both coexist. There is no test at the boundary (767px, 768px). A dev implementing with <= instead of < would pass all specified test widths but produce different behavior at the boundary.
warnings.proposed_fix: Add AC13 boundary test: 'GIVEN viewport width = 767px, THEN mobile layout is active (Candidates as tab, no fixed sidebar). GIVEN viewport width = 768px, THEN desktop layout is active (3-column with sidebar).' This removes implementation ambiguity about the boundary.

warnings.title: Budget recompute stale-response guard uses request_seq but specification does not define scope (per-day vs global)
warnings.description: M10/M25 both specify 'same stale-response guard (request_seq)' for budget recompute. The spec does not clarify whether request_seq is global or per-day. If the user switches between day 1 and day 2 rapidly, a global sequence counter would discard valid responses from day 2 if a stale day 1 response arrives later. A per-day counter avoids this but adds implementation complexity.
warnings.proposed_fix: Clarify AC25: 'The stale-response guard is per-day (each day maintains its own monotonic request_seq counter for budget recompute).' or 'The stale-response guard is global (a single counter; switching days increments it).'
